sections.headline: The Westin Monterrey Valle's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers.
sections.keyInsight: Westin Club is recognized in only 3.7% of monitored answers. That is low enough to matter commercially if the attribute is part of how the hotel should win relevant traveler needs. Holiday Inn Monterrey Valle also appears in related absent scenarios, which can compound the representation miss. Broader Scenario Presence (84.1%) and Consideration (42.5%) do not, by themselves, prove the distinctive attribute is traveling into answers.
sections.whyItMatters: If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on Westin Club. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.
sections.whatToReview: Open Reality Gap evidence for Westin Club and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named.
